symptom: In disposable Linux official CI #40509724807, 8000 bounded openat2 calls during concurrent real-directory rename yielded 3060 original single-link JSON reads, 131 real-kernel EAGAIN denials, 4809 ENOENT denials and no unexpected errors; the test passed without requiring a minimum EAGAIN count. This is not a production incident or proof of canonical publisher identity.
lesson: Actual Linux openat2 may emit EAGAIN during concurrent real-directory rename with parent traversal. A bounded synthetic observer can verify permitted denial classes and original bytes without asserting a flaky minimum EAGAIN count. A deterministic injected EAGAIN contract and real-kernel observation establish different, complementary evidence.
guardrail: Treat openat2 EAGAIN as indeterminate and fail closed: no unbounded retry, pathname fallback, stale-path cleanup, or inferred publisher identity. Keep bounded aggregate errno observations diagnostic only, never readiness statistics. Reuse the pinned root FD and traversal constraints solely as path-resolution guards; independently review common reader/writer directory authority, mount changes, power-loss durability and recovery before any native integration. No protected N2, BUY, LINE, public or production authority.
